# Operator Reference

Every operator in qex, one line each, linked to its entry: its signature, what it does, how it treats missing
values, and examples, most worked on the [toy data](toy-data.md).

In the signatures:

- `x`, `y` are expressions: anything that gives a value per date and stock;
- `period`, `n`, `window`, `halflife` are whole numbers of days or values; `q`, `limit` are numbers;
- `'name'` is a quoted field or group name; `groups` is a group's name or any expression giving labels;
- `[, arg]` is an optional argument.

## Data and primitives

[Data and primitives in detail →](ops/data.md)

- [`close()`](ops/data.md#close): Each stock's closing price, adjusted for splits and dividends
- [`open()`](ops/data.md#close): Opening price, adjusted
- [`high()`](ops/data.md#close): Daily high, adjusted
- [`low()`](ops/data.md#close): Daily low, adjusted
- [`field('name')`](ops/data.md#field): Any field of the data by name, read as numbers (read labels with `group('name')`)
- [`market()`](ops/data.md#market): The market's price level: the data's `market` series, the same for every stock
- [`returns(period[, 'field'])`](ops/data.md#returns): Return over `period` days, of `close` or another price field: p[t] / p[last price at or before t − period] − 1
- [`volatility(period[, 'field'])`](ops/data.md#volatility): Annualized volatility: the standard deviation of daily returns over `period` days, times √252. Part of the window
- [`volume(period)`](ops/data.md#volume): Average daily volume over `period` days, in shares. Part of the window
- [`adv(period)`](ops/data.md#adv): Average daily dollar volume, close × volume, over `period` days. Part of the window

## Math

[Math in detail →](ops/math.md)

- [`log(x)`](ops/math.md#log): Natural logarithm; missing for x ≤ 0 (−inf at 0)
- [`exp(x)`](ops/math.md#exp): e to the `x`, the inverse of `log`; inf when too large
- [`abs(x)`](ops/math.md#abs): Absolute value
- [`sign(x)`](ops/math.md#sign): −1, 0 or 1
- [`sqrt(x)`](ops/math.md#sqrt): Square root; missing for x < 0
- [`power(x, n)`](ops/math.md#power): `x` to the power `n`; `n` can be a number or an expression
- [`max(x, y)`](ops/math.md#max): The larger of `x` and `y`, element by element
- [`min(x, y)`](ops/math.md#min): The smaller of `x` and `y`, element by element

## Time series

Each stock's own history. Each operator follows one of three [window rules](ops/time-series.md#window-rules). [Time series in detail →](ops/time-series.md)

### Rolling statistics

- [`ts_mean(x, period)`](ops/time-series.md#ts_mean): Mean over the last `period` days. Part of the window
- [`ts_std(x, period)`](ops/time-series.md#ts_std): Standard deviation over the window. Part of the window
- [`ts_sum(x, period)`](ops/time-series.md#ts_sum): Sum over the window. Part of the window
- [`ts_max(x, period)`](ops/time-series.md#ts_max): Largest value in the window. Part of the window
- [`ts_min(x, period)`](ops/time-series.md#ts_min): Smallest value in the window. Part of the window
- [`ts_var(x, period)`](ops/time-series.md#ts_var): Variance over the window. Part of the window
- [`ts_quantile(x, period, q[, min_periods])`](ops/time-series.md#ts_quantile): The `q`-quantile of the window, `q` from 0 to 1: 0.5 is the median, 0 and 1 are `ts_min` and `ts_max`. Part of the window

### Lag and difference

- [`delay(x, period)`](ops/time-series.md#delay): The value `period` days ago; `period` ≥ 0
- [`delta(x, period)`](ops/time-series.md#delta): Today's value minus the value `period` days ago: `x - delay(x, period)`

### Ranking and extremes

- [`ts_rank(x, period)`](ops/time-series.md#ts_rank): Today's percentile among the last `period` values, from 1/period to 1; ties share their average rank. The whole window
- [`ts_argmax(x, period)`](ops/time-series.md#ts_argmax): Days since the largest value in the window, 0 if it is today. The whole window
- [`ts_argmin(x, period)`](ops/time-series.md#ts_argmin): Days since the smallest value in the window. The whole window

### Pairs of series

Regressions and correlations through time: one fit per stock, over its own window. For a regression across
the stocks on each day, see `regression_neut` under Cross-sectional.

- [`ts_corr(x, y, period[, min_periods])`](ops/time-series.md#ts_corr): Correlation of `x` and `y` over the window. Part of the window
- [`ts_cov(x, y, period[, min_periods])`](ops/time-series.md#ts_cov): Covariance over the window. Part of the window
- [`ts_beta(y, x, period[, min_periods])`](ops/time-series.md#ts_beta): Least-squares slope of `y` on `x`, cov(y, x) / var(x), over the window. Part of the window
- [`ts_beta_shrunk(y, x, period[, min_periods][, groups])`](ops/time-series.md#ts_beta_shrunk): `ts_beta`, pulled toward the day's average beta (or with `groups`, its group's) in proportion to its noise (Vasicek). Part of the window
- [`ts_alpha(y, x1, ..., xk, period[, min_periods])`](ops/time-series.md#ts_alpha): Intercept of `y` on one or more regressors over the window, from one joint least-squares fit on the days all have a value; with one, mean(y) − beta × mean(x). Part of the window
- [`ts_alpha_shrunk(y, x, period[, min_periods][, groups])`](ops/time-series.md#ts_alpha_shrunk): The intercept that goes with `ts_beta_shrunk`'s slope. Part of the window
- [`ts_resid(y, x1, ..., xk, period[, min_periods])`](ops/time-series.md#ts_resid): Today's residual from the window's fit, y − alpha − Σ beta_j × x_j: the part of today's `y` the regressors don't explain. Part of the window
- [`ts_resid_shrunk(y, x, period[, min_periods][, groups])`](ops/time-series.md#ts_resid_shrunk): Today's residual from `ts_beta_shrunk`'s fit. Part of the window

### Exponentially weighted

- [`ewma(x, halflife)`](ops/time-series.md#ewma): Exponentially weighted mean: a day's weight halves every `halflife` days. Exponential
- [`ewma_var(x, halflife)`](ops/time-series.md#ewma_var): Exponentially weighted variance. Exponential
- [`ewma_cov(x, y, halflife)`](ops/time-series.md#ewma_cov): Exponentially weighted covariance. Exponential
- [`ts_beta_ewma(y, x, halflife)`](ops/time-series.md#ts_beta_ewma): ewma_cov(y, x) / ewma_var(x), over the days both have a value. Exponential

### Shape of the window

- [`ts_skew(x, period)`](ops/time-series.md#ts_skew): Skewness of the window. The whole window
- [`ts_kurt(x, period)`](ops/time-series.md#ts_kurt): Excess kurtosis of the window. The whole window
- [`decay_linear(x, period)`](ops/time-series.md#decay_linear): Weighted mean with weights period, period − 1, ..., 1, newest heaviest. The whole window

## Events and state

[Events and state in detail →](ops/events.md)

- [`fill_forward(x[, limit])`](ops/events.md#fill_forward): Carry each value forward over the missing days after it, at most `limit` days; with no limit, until the next value
- [`latch(on, off)`](ops/events.md#latch): 1 from a day `on` is true until a day `off` is true (off wins a tie), then 0 until `on` again; 0 before `on` is first true; a day where either is missing changes nothing
- [`ts_mean_events(x, n[, min_n])`](ops/events.md#ts_mean_events): Mean of the last `n` values `x` has had, however far back; a value every day once there are `min_n` (default `n`)
- [`ts_std_events(x, n[, min_n])`](ops/events.md#ts_std_events): Standard deviation of the last `n` values, once there are `min_n`
- [`ts_sum_events(x, n[, min_n])`](ops/events.md#ts_sum_events): Sum of the last `n` values, once there are `min_n`
- [`ts_count_events(x, period)`](ops/events.md#ts_count_events): How many values `x` has in the last `period` days; an answer every day once `period` days have passed

## Cross-sectional

Across the stocks in the universe, one day at a time. [Cross-sectional in detail →](ops/cross-sectional.md)

- [`rank(x)`](ops/cross-sectional.md#rank): Percentile rank among the day's stocks, from 1/n to 1, lowest first; ties share their average rank
- [`zscore(x)`](ops/cross-sectional.md#zscore): (x − mean) / standard deviation across the day's stocks; missing when they don't vary
- [`gaussrank(x)`](ops/cross-sectional.md#gaussrank): The day's rank mapped through the inverse normal, Φ⁻¹((r − 0.5)/n): a z-score's shape without its outliers; ties share the average score, so each day sums to zero
- [`demean(x)`](ops/cross-sectional.md#demean): x minus the day's mean
- [`scale(x)`](ops/cross-sectional.md#scale): Divide by the day's sum of absolute values, so they sum to 1
- [`quantile(x, n)`](ops/cross-sectional.md#quantile): Bucket 1 (lowest) to `n` by percentile rank
- [`winsorize(x, limit)`](ops/cross-sectional.md#winsorize): Clip at the day's `limit` and 1 − `limit` quantiles: `winsorize(x, 0.05)` caps at the 5th and 95th percentiles
- [`truncate(x, max)`](ops/cross-sectional.md#truncate): Clip each value to [−max, max] (element by element, not across stocks)
- [`regression_neut(y, x1, x2, ...)`](ops/cross-sectional.md#regression_neut): One regression per day, across the stocks (not through time): `y` with its least-squares fit on the regressors (and an intercept) taken out
- [`regression_alpha(y, x1, ..., xk)`](ops/cross-sectional.md#regression_alpha): The intercept of `regression_neut`'s fit: one number per day, the same for every stock
- [`regression_beta(y, x1, ..., xk, j)`](ops/cross-sectional.md#regression_beta): The `j`-th slope of `regression_neut`'s fit: one number per day, the same for every stock; with one regressor `j` may be left out
- [`pca_factor(x, window, k[, refit])`](ops/cross-sectional.md#pca_factor): Each stock's beta to the k-th statistical factor of `x`, from a principal component analysis across stocks, refit every `refit` days (default 21)

## Groups

Within groups of stocks sharing a label, one day at a time. [Groups in detail →](ops/groups.md)

- [`group('name')`](ops/groups.md#group): The labels themselves, for comparing or grouping: `group('sector') == 'Technology'`
- [`identifier()`](ops/groups.md#identifier): Each stock's own identifier, as a label; through `ts_match`, its twin's
- [`group_cross(a, b, ...)`](ops/groups.md#group_cross): One grouping from several: labels joined with a bar, `'Technology|3'`
- [`group_demean(x, groups)`](ops/groups.md#group_demean): x minus its group's mean
- [`group_rank(x, groups)`](ops/groups.md#group_rank): Percentile rank within each group, from 1/n to 1
- [`group_gaussrank(x, groups)`](ops/groups.md#group_gaussrank): `gaussrank` within each group: normal scores among the group's stocks that day
- [`group_quantile(x, groups, n)`](ops/groups.md#group_quantile): Bucket 1 to `n` within each group: a dependent double sort
- [`group_std(x, groups)`](ops/groups.md#group_std): Standard deviation across the group's stocks that day; every member gets it
- [`group_sum(x, groups)`](ops/groups.md#group_sum): Sum within the group; every member gets it; missing when the group has no values that day
- [`group_count_valid(x, groups, period)`](ops/groups.md#group_count_valid): How many values the group's stocks have had over the last `period` days

## Matching

Each stock's statistical twin: one particular other stock, chosen from history. [Matching in detail →](ops/matching.md)

- [`ts_match(value, key, lookback, metric='corr', within=None, matching='nearest', rebalance=21, min_overlap=None)`](ops/matching.md#ts_match): The `value` of each stock's twin: the stock whose `key` over the last `lookback` days was most alike, chosen every `rebalance` days from the past only; options by name
- [`ts_match_score(key, lookback, metric='corr', within=None, matching='nearest', rebalance=21, min_overlap=None)`](ops/matching.md#ts_match_score): How alike each stock and its twin were when chosen: a correlation, or a distance for the distance metrics; reads the same selection as `ts_match`; options by name

## Logic and conditions

[Logic and conditions in detail →](ops/logic.md)

- [`where(cond, if_true, if_false)`](ops/logic.md#where): `if_true` where `cond` is nonzero, `if_false` where it is 0, missing where it is missing
- [`coalesce(x, y)`](ops/logic.md#coalesce): `x` where it has a value, else `y` (a number, label or expression)
- [`is_valid(x)`](ops/logic.md#is_valid): 1 where `x` has a value, else 0; an infinity counts as a value
- [`is_finite(x)`](ops/logic.md#is_finite): 1 where `x` is a finite number, 0 where it is missing or infinite
- `None`: No value here, on purpose: `where(cond, x, None)`

- `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`: Arithmetic, element by element
- `**`: Power, with a number as the exponent
- `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, `==`, `!=`: 1 or 0, missing where either side is missing
- `&`, `|`, `~`: And, or, not, three-valued

## Calendar

[Calendar in detail →](ops/calendar.md)

- [`day_of_week()`](ops/calendar.md#day_of_week): 0 (Monday) to 6 (Sunday)
- [`day_of_month()`](ops/calendar.md#day_of_month): 1 to 31
- [`month_of_year()`](ops/calendar.md#month_of_year): 1 to 12
